explanation

The stock DECLARE_CLASS named NCWnd as the super while the C++ base is NCNPCHtmlViewer (the stock Super:: is NCWnd); our header keeps the C++ base. The generated IMPLEMENT_CLASS takes the super from analysis/classes.json (docs/notas/Standalone.md, section 3).
The stock DECLARE_CLASS named NCWnd as the super while the C++ base is NCItemWnd; same case as NCTestHtmlViewer.

The stock DECLARE_CLASS named NCWnd as the super (classes.json super NCWnd) while the C++ base is NCDialogBox (its constructor 0x101229b0 calls the NCDialogBox one, 0x1000b350); same case as NCTestHtmlViewer.

The stock DECLARE_CLASS named NCWnd as the super while the C++ base is NCAbnormalStatusWnd (its constructor 0x101293b0 calls the NCAbnormalStatusWnd one, 0x10116530, with icon size 24); same case as NCTestHtmlViewer.

The stock DECLARE_CLASS named NCQuestWnd as the super while the C++ base is NCQuestGaraTreeWnd (its constructor 0x10090300 calls the NCQuestGaraTreeWnd one, 0x100ed2a0); same case as NCTestHtmlViewer. The generated IMPLEMENT_CLASS registers the stock parent.

The stock NCCmdTarget vtable has 39 slots (UObject 25 + NCCmdTarget 14); ours declares the 25 of the NCObject and NCWnd declares slots 25..38 (src/nwindow/NCWnd.cpp). NW_CHECK_VTABLE compares the 25 that exist.

Our NCCmdTarget declares no virtual of its own (25 slots, the NCObject ones), the stock 39 (slots 25..38 are declared in NCWnd here). NCCmdTarget is abstract and only NCWnd derives from it: its vtable is live only inside NCCmdTarget's constructor and destructor, which call no slot above 24.
The stock image emitted appMemcpy out of line (0x10001790) with an SSE branch on Core's GIsSSE; the standalone build has the C runtime's memcpy. Nothing else of the game code reads it.
Only the stock NL2Font constructor (0x1005b7a0) stores the intermediate FExec vtable (Core's) before its own; ours does not store it (docs/notas/Standalone.md, section 10).

Slot 25: the stock vtable points straight to NCButton::WindowProc (0x10021e60, the linker folded the override away); ours declares NCRadioButton::WindowProc (NCButton.cpp), whose body is `return NCButton::WindowProc(Msg, wParam, lParam) != 0`, the same result through one more frame.

Slot 25: the stock vtable points straight to NCButton::WindowProc (0x10021e60); ours inherits NCRadioButton::WindowProc, a body `return NCButton::WindowProc(...) != 0` (NCButton.cpp): the same result through one more frame.

Slot 25: the stock vtable points straight to NControl::WindowProc (0x10148f10); ours declares NCTabControl::WindowProc (NCTabControl.cpp), whose body is `return NControl::WindowProc(Msg, wParam, lParam) != 0`: the same result through one more frame.
Slot 49: the stock vtable points to NCWnd::HideWindow (0x10035ab0); ours declares NCMatchWnd::HideWindow (NCMatchWnd.cpp), whose body is `NCWnd::HideWindow()`: the same effect.

Slot 51: the stock vtable points to the NCWnd::OffsetWindow body (0x10035410: mov eax,[ecx]; jmp [eax+0x9c], i.e. virtual slot 39 MoveChildWindow); ours declares NCChatWnd::MoveWindow (NCChatWnd.cpp), whose body is `MoveChildWindow(DX, DY)`: the same call.

Slot 74: the stock vtable points to the 8-byte body at 0x100475f0 (8b 01 ff a0 2c 01 00 00: mov eax,[ecx]; jmp [eax+0x12c], a tail jump to virtual slot 75, CommitText) that the stock linker shared between several classes (the db names it after one of them, NCPlayerStatusWnd::Resize). Ours is NCHtmlEdit::GetValue / NCJHtmlEdit::GetValue (NCHtmlEdit.cpp, `return CommitText()`); the compiled standalone folds them into one function whose bytes (read in the DLL at its map address) are the same 8: mov eax,[ecx]; jmp [eax+0x12c]. Only the name differs.

Core's FString(INT, INT) (0x101572b0, ret 8) only stores three zero dwords at the object (mov eax,ecx; xor ecx,ecx; mov [eax],ecx; mov [eax+4],ecx; mov [eax+8],ecx): an empty string. The stock's game code calls it as FString(0, 1) for the empty result of a failed lookup, in two functions, NChatHeaderMap::Lookup (0x1014c490, at 0x1014c4ef) and NMsnIntStrMap::FindRef (0x10162be0, at 0x10162c23). Ours returns `FString()` in both (ChatWnd.cpp NChatHeaderMap::Lookup, NotificationProcess.cpp NMsnIntStrMap::FindRef), Core's default constructor (??0FString@@QAE@XZ, 0x1011c950, which this DLL imports): the same three zero stores. The same empty string, nothing dropped.

Core's FString(const char*) (0x1011caa0) builds the wide string of a narrow one (Num = Max = length + 1, then the converted characters). The stock's game code calls it in ten functions; each call was read in the stock (the literal pushed at the call): MsnCommand::ToString (0x1014bef0) the literal " "; NMsnGroup::SetName (0x101527b0) "%20" and " "; NChatSbSender::SendTyping (0x10152fe0) "U"; NChatSbSender::SendText (0x101530d0) "N"; SwitchboardSession::SendMSG (0x101531c0) "N"; NChatSbSender::SendInvite (0x101532b0) "CAL"; SwitchboardSession::AddFriend (0x101534e0) "NLN"; NChatNotifySender::RequestSwitchboard (0x10164910) "XFR" and "SB"; NotificationProcess::OnAsyncImpl (0x10165440) "FLN"; and NCInventoryWnd::ReadItemOrder (0x10098390), which appends FString(buf) for each byte of the character name, buf = _snprintf(buf, 3, "%d", byte ^ key). Ours builds the very same text in each of them: the nine literals with the wide constructor FString(const TCHAR*) from the same ASCII text (the conversion of ASCII is the identity and the wide constructor sets Num = Max = length + 1 too), and ReadItemOrder fills a TCHAR buffer with the same digits (same _snprintf, same key bytes 0xF5/0xA1, same re-evaluated strlen) and formats the same file name from it. Same strings, nothing dropped.

Core's FString::InStr(const FString&, INT) (0x101176e0) is a thunk: it loads the FString's data pointer (or Core's static empty L"" at 0x1021cf2c when the string is empty) and tail-jumps to InStr(const TCHAR*, INT) (0x10117600). The stock's NMsnStrReplaceImpl (0x10168890) calls it twice (at 0x101688f4 and 0x10168997) with Right = 0. Ours calls `Str->InStr(*From, 0)` at both places (ChatWnd.cpp NMsnStrReplaceImpl): FString::operator* gives the same data pointer or the same static empty string, and ?InStr@FString@@QBEHPBGH@Z is imported. The same call with the same arguments.
